name: Cutaneous Mastocytosis

prevalence.estimate: 1 per 10,000 in children (most common form); rarer in adults as isolated cutaneous disease
prevalence.range: Pediatric: 5-10 per 10,000; Adult isolated CM: <1 per 10,000

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Mastocytosis / ECNM Criteria

criteria.description: Typical skin lesions: maculopapular (urticaria pigmentosa), diffuse cutaneous, or mastocytoma
Positive Darier sign (urtication and wheal formation upon rubbing or stroking the lesion)
Skin biopsy confirming increased mast cell infiltration in the dermis
Absence of criteria for systemic mastocytosis (no bone marrow involvement, normal baseline tryptase or <20 ng/mL in children)
KIT mutation analysis (KIT D816V typically absent in pediatric CM; may be present in adult CM)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Typical skin lesions with histological confirmation of increased dermal mast cells, without evidence of systemic disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Pediatric CM often resolves spontaneously by adolescence. Adult CM should prompt bone marrow biopsy to exclude systemic mastocytosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Urticaria pigmentosa lesions with positive Darier sign
pathognomonic.notes: Brownish-red macules/papules that urticate when rubbed
searchTerms: skin lesions that swell when rubbed

common.symptomName: Blistering of lesions (in infants and young children)
common.notes: More common in very young children; resolves with age

rare.notes: Risk higher in diffuse cutaneous mastocytosis with large mast cell burden
Rare; raises concern for systemic disease

laboratory: Serum tryptase: usually normal or mildly elevated in CM; >20 ng/mL suggests systemic disease
imaging: No specific imaging findings for isolated CM
DEXA scan if adult with persistent disease (assess for osteoporosis)
genetic: KIT mutations in skin lesions (non-D816V mutations more common in pediatric CM)
KIT D816V may be present in adult CM (evaluate for systemic disease)
Pediatric CM is usually non-clonal or has non-D816V KIT mutations
other: Skin biopsy: increased mast cells in papillary dermis, often in perivascular distribution
Darier sign: urtication on mechanical irritation of a lesion
Bone marrow biopsy recommended in adults to exclude systemic mastocytosis

distinguishingFeatures: SM has bone marrow involvement with mast cell aggregates and KIT D816V
CM is limited to skin without systemic criteria met
Chronic urticaria has transient wheals that resolve within 24 hours
CM has fixed pigmented lesions that persist
Insect bites are transient and distributed differently
CM lesions are persistent and positive for Darier sign

redFlags: Adult-onset cutaneous mastocytosis (must exclude systemic disease with bone marrow biopsy)
Severe or extensive blistering in infants (risk of mediator-related symptoms)
Anaphylaxis episodes (consider systemic disease or high mast cell burden)
references: Hartmann K, et al. Cutaneous manifestations in patients with mastocytosis: consensus report of the European Competence Network on Mastocytosis. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2016;137(1):35-45.
Valent P, et al. Mastocytosis: 2016 updated WHO classification and novel emerging treatment concepts. Blood. 2017;129(11):1420-1427.
Carter MC, et al. Pediatric mastocytosis. Immunol Allergy Clin North Am. 2014;34(2):363-381.
